title: Three-tier memory architecture (foundational)
description: Signature original: Memory is organized in three tiers: a small fast working set for the current task, a larger summary tier of distilled findings, and the full archive of source records. Each tier has a fixed capacity and a defined promotion rule, which keeps the working set relevant without manual curation. This mirrors CPU cache hierarchies, where each level trades size for speed. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
tiers = {'working': {'cap': 5, 'items': []}, 'summary': {'cap': 50, 'items': []}, 'archive': {'cap': float('inf'), 'items': []}}
tiers['working']['items'] = ['w1', 'w2', 'w3']
print('working', len(tiers['working']['items']), '/', tiers['working']['cap'])
print('summary', len(tiers['summary']['items']), '/', tiers['summary']['cap'])
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Hierarchical Memory Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Promotion by reuse count (foundational)
description: Signature original: An item in the summary tier that gets reused across tasks is promoted to the working set, evicting the least-recently-used working item back down. Reuse is the promotion signal because it is direct evidence of value. Promotion and demotion keep the working set small but high-value without any manual triage. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
from collections import OrderedDict
working = OrderedDict([('w1', 1), ('w2', 1)])
working['w3'] = 3  # reused 3 times -> promote
working.move_to_end('w3')
evicted = working.popitem(last=False)
print('promoted: w3 | demoted:', evicted[0], '| working:', list(working))
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Hierarchical Memory Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Summary cascade on demotion (foundational)
description: Signature original: When a working item is demoted, it is not stored verbatim in the summary tier; it is first compressed to a one-line summary. The cascade keeps the summary tier dense: dozens of distilled findings fit where a few full items would. The original full record stays reachable in the archive tier via the summary's source link. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
def summarize(item):
    return item.split('.')[0][:60]
full = 'The inverted index cut query latency from 900ms to 40ms. Posting lists were the key change.'
print('summary-tier form:', summarize(full))
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Hierarchical Memory Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Capacity management with LRU eviction (foundational)
description: Signature original: Each tier enforces its capacity with least-recently-used eviction: the item untouched longest leaves first. LRU is chosen because it is simple, predictable, and matches the temporal locality of real task sequences. Evicted summary items are already represented in the archive tier, so nothing of value is truly lost. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
from collections import OrderedDict
tier = OrderedDict()
for k in ['a', 'b', 'c']: tier[k] = 1
tier['a'] = tier.pop('a')  # touch a -> most recent
tier['d'] = 1
if len(tier) > 3: tier.popitem(last=False)
print('after eviction:', list(tier), '(b evicted as LRU)')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Hierarchical Memory Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Tier-aware query routing (foundational)
description: Signature original: A query first checks the working set, then the summary tier, and only then the archive, stopping at the first tier that answers it. Routing by tier keeps common questions fast and reserves expensive archive searches for genuinely new questions. Each tier hit also refreshes that item's recency, reinforcing the LRU ordering. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Hierarchical Memory Manager, 2026-10-21.
